allow_options.description: AllowOptions are the telnet options a session may negotiate, by the names in docs/CONFIG.md. Default is the set an interactive session needs and nothing else. An option this proxy has no name for is always refused: one whose effect it cannot name is one it cannot hold to a policy.

banner.description: Banner replaces what the proxy says before the target is dialled. A banner naming the equipment is a banner that saves an attacker a question.

deception.description: Deception answers as a device that is not there: a login this listener was going to refuse answered by a fabricated shell, or a whole listener that is one. See TelnetDeception.

deny_options.description: DenyOptions removes from AllowOptions, for changing one thing without restating the list.

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_connections.description: MaxConnections bounds sessions on this listener. Default 1000.

mfa.description: MFA asks for a login name and a one-time code before the target is dialled. Telnet has no authentication of its own for a proxy to read, so this is a prompt the proxy writes and reads itself; the target's own login happens afterwards, unchanged.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol sends a PROXY protocol v2 header with the client address to the target.

recording.description: Recording writes the session -- what the target showed, and optionally what was typed -- to a file.

require_grant.description: RequireGrant admits a session only against a live grant from the access ledger: one somebody asked for, somebody else approved, and that ends by itself. Needs the access section. See docs/CONFIG.md.

session_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

upstream.description: Upstream is the pool of targets. Required.

ThreatIntel.description: ThreatIntel imports lists of client addresses and TLS fingerprints, each with its own action. It is deliberately not the ban list. A ban is earned here -- this proxy watched a client do something and decided -- while a list is imported and says nothing about what the client did *here*. That is why the default action is the careful one: a feed whose provenance an operator cannot check, with one wrong line in it, is an outage nobody can explain from the logs.

lists.description: Lists are the lists, in order. The first one that matches decides, so a narrow list belongs before the broad one it softens.

log_matches.description: LogMatches writes a security event for every match, including the ones whose action is log. Default true: a list nobody can see matching is a list nobody can tune.

refresh.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

action.description: Action is log (record it and serve the request), challenge (make the client prove it is a browser, which needs the challenge section) or block. Default log.

file.description: File holds the entries: one per line, with #, ; and // comments and a trailing comment after whitespace. A network may be written with host bits set; it is masked. Exactly one of file, url, taxii and misp is the source.

format.description: Format is how the source is written: lines (one indicator per line), stix (a STIX 2.1 bundle), misp (a MISP export) or auto. Default auto for a file or a url; a taxii source is always stix and a misp source always misp, and saying otherwise is refused. Naming it is better than letting it be sniffed. A feed whose format is named fails loudly when its publisher changes shape; a sniffed one quietly starts yielding nothing.

http.description: HTTP is how a network source is reached: the credential, the trust and the timeout. Ignored for a file.

kind.description: Kind is what the list is matched against: cidr client addresses and networks (the default) ja4 TLS client fingerprints domain host names, and every name under them url a host and path, matched at a path boundary hash MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 digests of a payload The first two are about who is connecting; the rest are about what the client asked for, which is a different question and often a better one.

misp.description: MISP is a MISP instance to search.

taxii.description: TAXII is a TAXII 2.1 collection to poll.

url.description: URL is a feed fetched over HTTP, conditionally: an unchanged feed costs a 304 rather than a download.

TokenExchange.description: TokenExchange is an RFC 8693 exchange at the token endpoint. A token the client sent to the gateway is a token the gateway forwards, and everything behind the gateway then holds a credential that works at the gateway. That is the confused-deputy problem in one sentence: a backend with a bug — a log line, an error page, an outbound request to somewhere it should not go — leaks a token that reaches the front door again with all of the client's scopes on it. Exchange replaces it. The proxy presents the verified client token to the authorization server and asks for one issued for *this* backend: a different audience, usually fewer scopes, and no standing anywhere else. The backend never sees the client's token, so there is nothing there to leak that would work at the gateway. The client's identity survives — the authorization server puts the same subject in the new token, which is what makes this an exchange rather than an impersonation.

required.description: Required refuses the request when the exchange fails. Default true: forwarding the client's token after failing to replace it would quietly undo the control on exactly the requests where it went wrong.

audience.description: Audience and Resource say who the new token is for: the backend's identifier at the authorization server, or its URI. At least one is required — an exchange that names neither asks for a token as broad as the one it replaces, which is the whole point undone.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the CA for the endpoint. Default: system pool.

cache_ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

client_id.description: ClientID and ClientSecretFile authenticate the proxy to the authorization server with HTTP basic authentication.

header.description: Header is where the new token goes. Default Authorization, as "Bearer <token>"; any other name carries the token alone.

requested_token_type.description: RequestedTokenType asks for a particular token type. Default: the authorization server's choice, which must be an access token or a JWT — a refresh token forwarded as an access token would be a long-lived credential handed to a backend.

scopes.description: Scopes asks for a subset. Empty leaves the decision to the authorization server, which will usually issue what the audience is entitled to.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

TokenIntrospection.description: TokenIntrospection is an RFC 7662 introspection endpoint.

always.description: Always introspects signed tokens too (revocation checks); default false introspects only tokens that are not JWS compact serialisations.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the CA for the endpoint. Default: system pool.

cache_ttl.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

client_id.description: ClientID and ClientSecretFile authenticate the proxy to the endpoint with HTTP basic authentication.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

Tracing.description: Tracing configures W3C trace context handling and span export.

enabled.description: Enabled defaults to true when the section is present.

otlp.description: OTLP exports spans; without it the context is only propagated and logged.

propagate.description: Propagate sends traceparent and tracestate to the upstream. Default true.

redact_client_address.description: RedactClientAddress runs a span's client.address through logging.redaction's client_ip rule. Default true. A span is not a log line, so nothing took it through the redactor: a deployment that turned redaction on to pseudonymise addresses still exported the full address to its trace collector, and the access log carries the trace id, so holding both stores reversed the pseudonymisation by design.

sample_percent.description: SamplePercent is the share of new traces (no incoming traceparent) that are recorded. Default 100.

trust_incoming.description: TrustIncoming honours the sampled flag of an incoming traceparent. Off (the default) the incoming trace id is continued for correlation but the sampling decision stays local, so a client cannot force every request into the exporter.

TransferICAP.description: TransferICAP scans the files a session moves (RFC 3507), for the kinds that move files rather than requests: ftp and sftp. A transfer is not an HTTP message, so the file is wrapped in the request or the response a scanner expects, which is what every ICAP scanner is built to read; the URL it sees names the real file, so a log at the scanner points at something an operator can find. Scanning holds the file: a verdict that arrives after the bytes is not a control. What that costs differs by protocol, and is written down under each listener.

downloads.description: Downloads scans the files a client fetches through RESPMOD. Default false, because a download doubles the bytes on the wire and most deployments trust what their own server already holds.

service.description: Service names an entry in icap.services. Required.

uploads.description: Uploads scans the files a client sends through REQMOD. Default true: a file arriving on a server is the direction that matters most.

UDPListener.description: UDPListener is a generic datagram relay: the symmetric primitive to kind: tcp for services whose protocol this proxy does not parse. A datagram has no connection, so the relay keeps a session table instead. The first datagram from a client address picks an endpoint through the pool's balancer and opens a connected socket towards it; every later datagram from that address goes to the same endpoint, and what the endpoint sends back goes to that address. The session ends when it has been idle, when it hits a bound, or at shutdown. Nothing in the payload is read: a kind: udp listener is a router and a set of bounds, not a parser. The thing to get right about a UDP relay is that it is a reflector. Anyone can put anybody's address in a datagram's source, so an open relay answers a victim with traffic the victim never asked for, at whatever gain the service behind it provides. That is why allow_clients and rate_limit exist here and why validation insists on one of them for a listener on a public address. The session table is bounded for the same reason: spoofed sources must not be able to fill it, which is what max_sessions_per_ip is for.

allow_clients.description: AllowClients restricts clients to these CIDRs. On a public address this or rate_limit is what stops the listener being somebody else's amplifier.

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_datagram_bytes.description: MaxDatagramBytes is the largest datagram relayed in either direction. Default 65535, which is the largest a UDP socket carries. A larger one is dropped and counted rather than truncated, because half a datagram is not a shorter datagram.

max_datagrams.description: MaxDatagrams bounds the datagrams of one session, both directions together. MaxBytesIn bounds what the session relays from the client and MaxBytesOut what it relays back, the same two names a kind: tcp listener uses. Past any of them the session ends and is counted. All default 0, no bound.

max_sessions.description: MaxSessions bounds the session table. Default 10000. A datagram from a new client when the table is full is dropped and counted: there is no way to refuse a datagram, because a refusal would be a datagram to an address that may not have sent anything.

max_sessions_per_ip.description: MaxSessionsPerIP bounds sessions from one address, which is what keeps a single source -- or a single forged source -- from filling the table. Default 64; 0 removes the bound.

rate_limit.description: RateLimit bounds datagrams per second from one source address. Without it a single source can drive the whole relay.

session_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

upstream.description: Upstream is the pool of endpoints. Required.

UDPRateLimit.description: UDPRateLimit bounds datagrams per second from one source address.

burst.description: Burst is how many may arrive at once. Default is PPS rounded up.

pps.description: PPS is datagrams per second. Required when the section is set.

Upstream.description: Upstream is a named pool of endpoints.

address_family.description: AddressFamily decides which of a dual-stack endpoint's addresses may be dialled: any (the default), ipv4 or ipv6. With any, the two families are raced as RFC 8305 describes -- the first family is tried, and after FallbackDelay the other is tried in parallel, with whichever connects first winning. That is what keeps a host whose IPv6 route is broken from costing a connect timeout on every request, and it is the default because an estate that has just turned IPv6 on should not have to know about it. ipv4 or ipv6 is for the estate where one family is the only one that works: it dials that family only, so a name with both kinds of record does not silently use the one the policy meant to exclude.

affinity.description: Affinity enables signed cookie session affinity.

balancer.description: Balancer is round_robin, weighted, least_conn or hash.

canary.description: Canary sends selected requests to endpoints marked canary.

circuit_breaker.description: CircuitBreaker stops sending to the pool as a whole after consecutive failures and probes it back with half open trials.

discovery.description: Discovery adds endpoints resolved from DNS (A/AAAA records of a name, or SRV records) and re-resolves them periodically. Static endpoints and discovered ones coexist; a pool needs at least one of the two.

fallback_delay.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

h2c.description: H2C speaks HTTP/2 without TLS to http endpoints (gRPC backends). Default false.

h3.description: H3 speaks HTTP/3 (QUIC) to https endpoints. Health probes use it too. Default false.

h3_fallback.description: H3Fallback retries a request over TCP (HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1) on the same endpoint when the QUIC connection cannot be established or fails before a response, so a network that drops UDP degrades to TCP rather than to errors. Default true.

hash_on.description: HashOn selects the hash input for the hash balancer: client_ip, header:<name> or cookie:<name>.

hedge.description: Hedge sends a second copy of an idempotent request to another endpoint when the first is slow, and takes whichever answers first, trading a little extra load for a shorter tail latency.

locality.description: Locality prefers the endpoints in this node's own zone.

maintenance.description: Maintenance takes the whole pool out of rotation: it offers no endpoint, so a route over it answers as it does when everything is unhealthy. For the planned outage of a whole service, where draining each endpoint would be a list to keep in step with the pool. As with an endpoint's drain, the management API overrides this until the daemon restarts.

max_concurrent.description: MaxConcurrent bounds requests in flight to the pool; 0 is unbounded.

max_connection_age.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_connections_per_endpoint.description: MaxConnectionsPerEndpoint is the default for every endpoint's own max_connections. An endpoint that names one uses that instead.

max_idle_conns_per_host.description: MaxIdleConnsPerHost bounds the pooled connections per endpoint.

origin_signature.description: OriginSignature signs every forwarded request with a key shared with the origin, so the origin can refuse traffic that did not pass through the proxy.

outlier_ejection.description: OutlierEjection removes endpoints that fail passively.

queue.description: Queue holds requests beyond MaxConcurrent for a bounded time.

retries.description: Retries is the number of times an idempotent request is retried on a connection error against a different endpoint. Default 1.

retry_budget.description: RetryBudget caps retries as a share of live traffic so a struggling pool is not buried under a retry storm. Without it every retry the Retries budget allows is sent.

retry_on.description: RetryOn adds response statuses that are retried like connection errors, on another endpoint, within the same Retries budget and only for replayable requests: "5xx", "500", "502", "503", "504", "429". A retried status counts as a passive failure of the endpoint. Default none.

scheme.description: Scheme is http or https. Default http.

slow_start.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

UpstreamQueue.description: UpstreamQueue bounds the requests waiting for a MaxConcurrent slot.

size.description: Size is the number of waiting requests; more are refused at once.

timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

UpstreamTLS.description: UpstreamTLS configures TLS towards upstream endpoints.

client_cert_file.description: ClientCertFile / ClientKeyFile enable mTLS to the upstream. The pair is re-read by reload-certs and by configuration reload.

insecure_skip_verify.description: InsecureSkipVerify disables verification. Refused unless allow_insecure is also true; logged as a security warning at start.

key_exchange.description: KeyExchange is the offered key agreement groups in preference order, as in the listener section. Empty means the default.

spki_pins.description: SPKIPins are base64 SHA-256 digests of the upstream leaf public key (as in HTTP Public Key Pinning). When set, the connection is refused unless the presented leaf matches one pin, in addition to chain verification.

UpstreamTimeout.description: UpstreamTimeout bounds each phase of an upstream exchange.

connect.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

idle.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

response_header.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

total.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

VNCBounds.description: VNCBounds bound the pixel stream: what the desktop may declare, and therefore what the viewer at the other end is asked to allocate. Image protocols are where a decompression bomb is cheapest to send. A rectangle's header is twelve bytes and says how many pixels it covers; a viewer sizes its decode buffer from that. A desktop that says 4096x4096 in twelve bytes of zlib is asking for sixty-four megabytes, and it can ask again immediately. None of these bounds requires decompressing anything: they compare what was declared with what arrived. A zero field is no bound.

max_cut_text.description: MaxCutText bounds one clipboard transfer in either direction, in bytes. Default 1048576.

max_decode_ratio.description: MaxDecodeRatio bounds the declared picture over the bytes that carry it, for the compressed encodings. Default 1000: a thousandfold is past any real screen and well short of what a bomb needs to be worth sending.

max_encoded_rectangle.description: MaxEncodedRectangle bounds one rectangle's encoded payload in bytes. Default 16777216.

max_framebuffer_pixels.description: MaxFramebufferPixels bounds the desktop size, in pixels: the one the target announces, the one a resize changes it to, and the one a client asks for. Default 33177600, which is 7680x4320.

max_rectangles_per_update.description: MaxRectanglesPerUpdate bounds one framebuffer update's rectangles. Default 4096. A thousand one-pixel rectangles cost the viewer a thousand decode calls for one screen.

VNCListener.description: VNCListener is a VNC gateway: the proxy is an RFB server to the client and an RFB client to the target, terminating the handshake of RFC 6143 on both legs. The reason it is not a tcp listener: RFB's whole policy surface is in the handshake. Which security type is used, whether the session is encrypted and how, what the desktop is called -- all of it is negotiated in the first few hundred bytes, and a proxy that does not sit in that negotiation cannot decide any of it, nor record what follows.

allow_clients.description: AllowClients restricts clients to these CIDRs.

allow_resize.description: AllowResize lets a client ask the desktop to change size (SetDesktopSize). Default true. The size asked for is bounded by Bounds.MaxFramebufferPixels whatever this says, because a client asking a desktop to allocate a framebuffer is the same attack in the other direction.

bounds.description: Bounds bound what the desktop may ask the viewer to allocate.

clipboard.description: Clipboard says which way a clipboard transfer may travel: both (the default), to_client, to_target or none. A bastion whose sessions are recorded usually wants to_client at most: a clipboard into the desktop is an upload with no name and no size in the log.

handshake_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

idle_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

max_connections.description: MaxConnections bounds sessions on this listener. Default 200.

mfa.description: MFA asks for a login name and a one-time code before the target is dialled.

password_file.description: Password is a file holding the VNC password this proxy answers its own vncauth challenge with. Without it, vncauth towards the client is refused: a challenge nobody can answer is not authentication.

pixel_stream.description: PixelStream says whether the gateway reads the desktop's picture. framed (the default) reads every message the desktop sends and every rectangle inside it, which is what makes Bounds possible: an image protocol's numbers are the viewer's allocations, and a gateway that forwards them unread cannot refuse one that is a bomb. It also decides what a client may ask for, because framing needs every encoding in play to be one the gateway can measure, so the encodings it cannot are removed from the client's list and the desktop never uses them -- tight among them. opaque forwards the desktop's bytes without reading them, which is what a listener that must have tight sets. Only the announced framebuffer size is then bounded; the rest of Bounds cannot be. The client's own messages are framed either way, because that is what lets a gateway refuse one and forward the next.

proxy_protocol.description: ProxyProtocol sends a PROXY protocol v2 header to the target.

recording.description: Recording writes the RFB stream to a file.

require_grant.description: RequireGrant admits a session only against a live grant from the access ledger: one somebody asked for, somebody else approved, and that ends by itself. Needs the access section. See docs/CONFIG.md.

rsa_key_file.description: RSAKeyFile is the RSA private key this proxy presents in the rsa-aes security types. Required with any of them, in PEM, PKCS#1 or PKCS#8, and at least 2048 bits.

security_types.description: SecurityTypes are the RFB security types a client may use, by name. Default is the ones this proxy mediates: none, vncauth and vencrypt. A type not listed is refused.

session_timeout.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

ssh.description: SSH reaches the target through an SSH connection this proxy makes, so the RFB never crosses the network in clear. This is the usual way a VNC server is reached safely, done by the gateway rather than by every operator.

tls_mode.description: TLSMode says what the listener's tls section is for. negotiated (the default) leaves the socket plain and presents the certificate inside RFB, which is what VeNCrypt does and what a modern viewer offers by itself. wrap makes the socket TLS from the first byte, with RFB inside it, which is what a viewer reaching an stunnel-wrapped port expects. A port is one or the other and cannot be both: the first byte a client sends is either a TLS record or "RFB 003.008".

upstream.description: Upstream is the pool of targets. Required.

upstream_password_file.description: UpstreamPasswordFile is the password this proxy uses towards the target, when the target asks for vncauth.

upstream_rsa_fingerprint.description: UpstreamRSAFingerprint pins the target's rsa-aes public key. Required to use rsa-aes towards a target: nothing else authenticates the far end of that exchange, and there is nobody at a proxy to show a fingerprint to. The log prints the key a target offered, which is how this gets filled in.

upstream_security.description: UpstreamSecurity is the security type to prefer towards the target, by name. Default is the strongest the target offers among the ones this proxy mediates.

upstream_tls.description: UpstreamTLS pins the CA and name for the target's leg.

upstream_tls_mode.description: UpstreamTLSMode is none or vencrypt. Default none.

upstream_user.description: UpstreamUser is the login this proxy presents to a target whose security type carries a name, which among the types here means MS-Logon II. Its password is UpstreamPasswordFile.

vencrypt_subtypes.description: VeNCryptSubtypes are the VeNCrypt subtypes offered when vencrypt is in SecurityTypes. Default x509-vnc and x509-none, which are the ones with a certificate to check.

view_only.description: ViewOnly drops the client's pointer and keyboard messages, so a session can be watched and not driven.

VNCOverSSH.description: VNCOverSSH reaches a VNC target through an SSH connection the gateway makes itself.

address.description: Address is the SSH host, host:port. Default is the upstream endpoint's host with port 22.

key_file.description: KeyFile is the private key the gateway authenticates with. Required.

known_hosts.description: KnownHosts pins the SSH host keys. Required: an unpinned tunnel authenticates nothing, which is the whole reason for the tunnel.

target.description: Target is what to reach from the SSH host, host:port. Default 127.0.0.1:5900, which is where a VNC server bound to loopback is.

user.description: User is the login on the SSH host. Required.

VaultSecrets.description: VaultSecrets is the Vault a vault: reference reads from. Only reading is implemented, and deliberately: a proxy that could write to the vault would be a proxy whose compromise rewrites the estate's secrets.

address.description: Address is the API base. https unless insecure is set, because http hands the token and every secret to the network.

ca_file.description: CAFile pins the authority the server's certificate is checked against; empty uses the system pool. ServerName overrides the name verified.

insecure.description: Insecure allows http and skips verification, and needs allow_insecure as well: one flag is a typo, two are a decision.

kv_version.description: KVVersion is 2 (the default) or 1. They differ in the request path and in where the fields sit in the answer, and guessing between them answers "not found" for a secret that is there.

mount.description: Mount is the KV mount a reference uses when it names none. Default "secret".

namespace.description: Namespace is the Vault Enterprise namespace, sent as a header. Without it an estate that uses namespaces gets "not found" for every secret.

token_file.description: TokenFile holds the token, and TokenEnv names an environment variable holding it. Exactly one is required. A token in this document would be a token in the management dump, the history and every diff; a token in the environment is readable by more than this process, which is why it is warned about.

VirtualPatch.description: VirtualPatch blocks a known vulnerability by its request shape while the application is being fixed: every listed condition must hold for the patch to apply. Patches run right after route matching, before rate limits, filters and the WAF, so they cost nothing for other traffic and work without a WAF section.

action.description: Action is block (default) or log.

body.description: Body matches the request body (buffered up to max_bytes and replayed to the upstream).

enabled.description: Enabled false keeps the patch in the configuration without applying it. Default true.

expires.description: Expires disables the patch after this date (RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD) so a temporary measure does not outlive the fix unnoticed; the status shows expired patches.

hosts.description: Hosts and Routes narrow the patch to host patterns (exact or "*.example.com") and route names. Empty means every host or route.

id.description: ID names the patch in logs, status and metrics (for example cve-2024-1234).

methods.description: Methods narrows the patch to these methods.

paths.description: Paths are prefixes of the cleaned path; PathRegex patterns match the whole path. At least one condition among paths, path_regex, query, headers, cookies and body is required.

query.description: Query, Headers and Cookies are conditions on parameters, header fields and cookies: the name must be present and, with a pattern, some value must match it.

status.description: Status is the response for block. Default 403.

WAF.description: WAF configures the web application firewall engine.

anomaly.description: Anomaly detects clients whose behaviour departs from the population (request rate, rule match ratio, error ratio, path spread) rather than requests that match a rule.

default_mode.description: DefaultMode applies to routes without a waf block: off, detect or block. Default block when the section is present.

default_profile.description: DefaultProfile applies to routes without a waf block. Default "default".

inspect_responses.description: InspectResponses enables response header and body inspection.

learning.description: Learning collects the variables that trigger detection rules and proposes exclusions (GET /v1/waf, xproxyctl waf proposals).

request_body_limit.description: RequestBodyLimit bounds the request body inspected. Default 1 MiB.

request_body_limit_action.description: RequestBodyLimitAction is reject (413) or partial (inspect the first RequestBodyLimit bytes and pass the rest). Default reject.

response_body_limit.description: ResponseBodyLimit bounds the response body inspected. Default 512 KiB; larger bodies are passed uninspected.

response_mime_types.description: ResponseMIMETypes lists content types whose bodies are inspected.

WAFAnomaly.description: WAFAnomaly tunes behavioural anomaly detection. Every WAF protected request is attributed to its client; at the end of each window the clients' feature vectors update a population baseline (mean and variance per feature) and a client whose largest z-score reaches the threshold is flagged until it looks normal again.

action.description: Action for requests of a flagged client: log, challenge or block. Default log.

max_clients.description: MaxClients bounds the tracked clients per window. Default 65536.

min_requests.description: MinRequests is the number of requests a client needs in a window before it is scored. Default 30.

threshold.description: Threshold is the z-score at which a client is flagged. Default 4.

window.description: Go duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m or 1h; empty or omitted means the default

WAFJSONSchema.description: WAFJSONSchema binds a schema file to request paths.

required.description: Required rejects requests under Paths without a JSON body. Default false: a request without a body or with another media type passes to the rules.

methods.description: Methods restricts enforcement to these methods. Default POST, PUT and PATCH.

paths.description: Paths are the request path prefixes the schema applies to.

schema_file.description: SchemaFile is a JSON Schema document (JSON or YAML).

WAFLearning.description: WAFLearning tunes exclusion learning. Matches are aggregated per rule, target variable and route across block and detect mode alike; a triple seen min_hits times becomes a proposal.

max_entries.description: MaxEntries bounds the learning table. Default 10000.

min_hits.description: MinHits is the number of matches before a proposal appears. Default 5.

WAFProfile.description: WAFProfile is a named rule set.

crs.description: CRS enables the OWASP Core Rule Set bundled with the binary.

directive_files.description: DirectiveFiles are SecLang files loaded after the CRS setup and before the CRS rules (the right place for exclusions).

directives.description: Directives is inline SecLang loaded in the same position.

json_schemas.description: JSONSchemas enforce a JSON Schema on request bodies under a path prefix, before the rules run.

WebSocketGuard.description: WebSocketGuard is the frame policy of an upgraded connection. Every bound applies to both directions; the rate applies to the client, whose traffic the estate does not control.

action.description: Action is close or log. Default close.

allow_opcodes.description: AllowOpcodes names the opcodes a peer may use. Default text, binary, close, ping and pong.

close_code.description: CloseCode overrides the close code sent on a violation.

deny_patterns.description: DenyPatterns are RE2 patterns matched against inspected messages.

inspect.description: Inspect is none, text or all: which messages are kept for pattern matching. Default text.

max_frame_bytes.description: MaxFrameBytes is the largest single frame. Default 1 MiB.

max_inspect_bytes.description: MaxInspectBytes bounds the prefix of a message kept for matching. Default 64 KiB.

max_message_bytes.description: MaxMessageBytes is the largest reassembled message. Default 8 MiB.

messages_per_second.description: MessagesPerSecond bounds the client's message rate. 0 is no bound.

require_masked.description: RequireMasked enforces RFC 6455 masking: set on client frames, clear on server frames. Default true.

validate_utf8.description: ValidateUTF8 refuses a text message that is not UTF-8. Default true.

YARAPolicy.description: YARAPolicy applies YARA rules to a stream. The engine is a subset of the language implemented in Go — this proxy links no C library into the data plane — and what it supports is listed in the reference; anything outside it is refused at load rather than quietly matching nothing. On a stream, two things differ from scanning a file. A rule is reported the first time its condition becomes true, because a decision that arrives after the last byte is a decision about a transfer that already happened. And filesize means the bytes seen so far, which is the only honest reading when there is no end yet.

action.description: Action on a match: close (the default) ends the connection, log records it and lets the bytes through.

directions.description: Directions are the sides scanned: client (what the client sends) and upstream (what comes back). Default both. Scanning one side halves the work where only one carries what the rules are about.

max_bytes.description: MaxBytes stops scanning a direction after this many bytes; the connection carries on unscanned. 0 scans everything. Default 33554432, which covers the start of a transfer without turning a long download into unbounded work.

max_window.description: MaxWindow is the buffer one direction scans in. It also bounds the overlap carried between windows, which is what lets a match straddling two reads still be found. Default 262144.

rules_file.description: RulesFile or RulesDir is where the rules are. Exactly one is required. A directory takes every .yar and .yara file in it, in name order, as one set.
